brief.headline: AI still takes about 64% of venture dollars, but the fastest-growing new themes are physical: robotics, defence, space and power
brief.summary: Q3 2026 global venture reached $159bn (+53% YoY; down from Q2's record $212bn), with AI at $102bn (64%) and a record 27 rounds of $1bn+ (Crunchbase). Capital is concentrating: late stage took $105bn and early stage $40.6bn. Outside software, physical AI ($47.4bn in H1), defence (a record by June), space ($20.8bn in Q3, a record) and power for AI (fusion and fission mega-rounds) are compounding fastest. For an LP: deploy EARLY where specialists see the frontier before mega-rounds (physical AI applications, defence autonomy, nuclear and grid, agent security, vertical agents). In GROWTH, be selective and favour category leaders bought via tenders or secondaries over primary rounds priced for perfection.

playbook.title: Weekly (15 min): this tab + one deal digest
playbook.detail: Read the Trends brief and heat changes here, then scan one weekly round-up (Crunchbase "week's biggest rounds" or aifunding.me). Flag any theme whose heat moved by 5 or more for a deeper look.

playbook.title: Quarterly benchmarks (block 2 hours when they drop)
playbook.detail: Crunchbase quarterly global funding, PitchBook-NVCA Venture Monitor, CB Insights State of Venture; plus sector trackers: Seraphim (space), FIA (fusion, annual), Menlo enterprise AI (annual, Nov), State of AI (Oct).

playbook.title: GP voices: 2-3 long-form interviews a week
playbook.detail: 20VC, Invest Like the Best, BG2 (Gerstner/Gurley), No Priors, Dwarkesh, Acquired and the a16z podcast. Note when two or more top GPs independently name the same theme: that is the earliest consensus signal.

playbook.title: Use your GPs as sensors
playbook.detail: Ask each GP: "Which theme is your partnership most over- and under-weight, and where are you seeing the highest entry prices?" Log answers as comments on the GP in Atlas. Cross-check against their portfolio additions in the Changes tab.

playbook.title: Specialist access for physical / frontier themes
playbook.detail: Physical AI, defence, space, energy and quantum reward specialist GPs (e.g. Lux, Eclipse, DCVC, Founders Fund, 8VC, Playground) and co-invest rights. Prefer funds where you get co-invest flow in your L1 themes.

playbook.title: Primary checks before IC
playbook.detail: Expert calls (AlphaSense / Tegus / GLG), customer references, and secondary pricing (Forge, Caplight) to test whether the theme narrative shows up in revenue. Use Shortlisted to track names you would back across rounds.

playbook.title: Keep a thesis with kill criteria per theme
playbook.detail: In each theme's note, write the 2-3 milestones that would make you overweight, and the ones that would make you stop. Refresh the theme before an IC to check them.

themes.name: Frontier models & AI labs
themes.summary: The labs building frontier models (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, xAI) plus well-funded challengers. Revenue is compounding faster than any software category on record, and labs now capture most enterprise AI spend.
themes.why_now: State of AI 2026 puts the combined OpenAI + Anthropic revenue run-rate at about $105bn (from about $30bn at the start of the year). Menlo Ventures finds Anthropic, OpenAI and Google take 69% of enterprise AI deployment dollars, with Anthropic at 55% of enterprise API spend.
themes.deploy_view: Growth only, and only at entry prices that still compound: tenders and primary rounds in the two leaders, accessed directly or via low-fee SPVs. Seed-stage "neo-labs" now price at multi-billion valuations (Thinking Machines, SSI, Reflection), so they are not early-stage risk/return. Avoid fee-stacked SPV layers.
